_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face. The pursuer's target sits 190 wu west of the hill and 40 wu below its bottom edge, so its leg is clear of the hill and it charges straight east. Measured with a 2-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 120, the charge makes contact at tick 159 and drives the router back about 60 wu west, the two fight one unbroken melee, and the router routs at tick 343. It stays ROUTING to the end of the clip, drifting south (from y 620 to about 770) and staying over 200 wu clear of the hill as its morale recovers. The pursuer's facing turns smoothly through the charge, with no snap larger than 20 degrees between 2-tick samples. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill: the router's flight never meets it. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. After the rout the pursuer gallops after the router and its own block deforms (a dense scan reads shape residual up to about 176 wu after tick 343), so the declared checks pin the router's story beats with only three sparse post-rout samples (400, 560 and 680) rather than sampling the gallop densely.
